# Beak

> Beak is a configuration-driven admin framework for Dart and Flutter. Annotated schema classes generate typed field references such as ProductModel.name, a Shelf REST API with graph commits, migrations and a Flutter panel built from BeakResource screens. Users never write string field references or touch dynamic.

## Start

- [Beak](index.md): Beak builds an admin panel, a REST API and migrations for Dart and Flutter from annotated schema classes and declarative resources.
- [What is Beak?](start-here/what-is-beak.md): Build Dart and Flutter admin interfaces from shared model and screen configuration.
- [Why Beak?](start-here/why-beak.md): Understand where declarative configuration reduces repeated admin work.
- [Installation](start-here/installation.md): Install the Beak CLI and scaffold your first admin panel. No Docker, no database to set up.
- [Quickstart](start-here/quickstart.md): Generate and run the minimal maintained Beak application.
- [Project structure](start-here/project-structure.md): Separate model behavior, resource navigation and screen layout in one application.
- [Two ways to boot a panel](start-here/generated-or-authored.md): Choose between the generated BeakApp and an authored BeakPanel, and switch with beak eject main.
- [Choose your path](start-here/paths/index.md): Pick the starting situation that matches your project and follow its first pages.
- [A new project](start-here/paths/new-project.md): Make the first decisions of a greenfield project: database, entrypoint and authentication.
- [An existing database](start-here/paths/existing-database.md): Point Beak at a database you already have and review the schemas it introspects.
- [An existing Flutter app](start-here/paths/existing-flutter-app.md): Mount a Beak panel inside a Flutter app you already have and share its session.
- [An existing Serverpod project](start-here/paths/existing-serverpod-project.md): Route an existing Serverpod project to the admin app or to the client bridge.
- [An existing backend](start-here/paths/existing-backend.md): Keep your REST or RPC backend and let the Beak panel talk to it.
- [Contributing to Beak](start-here/paths/contributing.md): Clone the repository, get the gate green and pick work to do.
- [Upgrading](start-here/upgrading.md): Map the old generated-panel APIs to the current declarative ones, in migration order.

- [Dynamic attributes and variants](models/dynamic-attributes-and-variants.md): Share attribute metadata between editors and validation, then preview and stage variant combinations.
- [The panel](panel/index.md): Compose resource screens, workflows and custom pages.

- [Navigation](panel/navigation.md): Build navigation from resources and custom pages.

- [Composed lists and query state](panel/composed-lists.md): Share one typed query across list presets, filters, summaries, saved views and exports.
- [View modes](panel/view-modes.md): Keep shared model behavior while choosing a task-specific presentation.
- [Actions](panel/actions.md): Expose model transitions and typed bulk edits with automatic validation and persistence.
- [Overlays](panel/overlays.md): Open confirmations, modals, dialogs, side sheets and toasts from an action context.
- [Custom screens](panel/custom-screens.md): Compose dashboards and complete custom application screens from Beak blocks and widgets.
- [Dashboards](panel/dashboards.md): Combine live queries, aggregates and custom widgets on a page.
- [Auth and idle-lock](panel/auth-and-idle-lock.md): Configure Beak-owned login, registration and password recovery over one backend session authority.
- [Maintenance and coming soon](panel/maintenance-and-coming-soon.md): Use dedicated presentation states while controlling service access separately.
- [Forms and records](forms/index.md): Route between form screens, inputs, related records, wizards, detail views, drafts and uploads.
- [Form screens](forms/form-screens.md): Use one declarative form runtime for values, rules, related drafts and saves.
- [Inputs](forms/inputs.md): Choose an input for each field type: text, numbers, currency, dates, choices, tags and ranges.
- [Related records in forms](forms/related-records.md): Edit related records in a form with comboboxes, search, cards, table editors and staged changes.
- [Multi-step forms](forms/multi-step-forms.md): Present one managed draft in validated steps.
- [Workflow presentations](forms/workflow-presentations.md): Compose wizard regions, rich choices, catalog editors and read presentations over one managed draft.
- [Detail views](forms/detail-views.md): Reuse a structured layout to read, edit and create records, with record blocks and relation managers.
- [Drafts, review and conflicts](forms/drafts-and-review.md): Resume local work, inspect pending changes and resolve concurrent edits.
- [Uploads and galleries](forms/uploads-and-galleries.md): Stage uploads and ordered image collections in ordinary declarative form drafts.
- [Imports and bulk edits](forms/imports-and-bulk-edits.md): Preview typed CSV input and mass changes through the graph save protocol.
- [Printable record documents](forms/record-documents.md): Configure an authorized persisted record document with typed values and related-row tables.
- [Blocks and charts](blocks/index.md): Compose custom page content from typed descriptions.

- [The backend](backend/index.md): See what the generated server gives you: routes, layers and the pages that configure each part.
- [Running the server](backend/running-the-server.md): Run the generated Shelf host, configure it, and test the same API in isolation.
- [Databases](backend/databases.md): Run on SQLite by default, or point DATABASE_URL at Postgres.
- [Migrations](backend/migrations.md): Create schemas from model metadata and evolve existing data with explicit migrations.
- [Seeding](backend/seeding.md): Populate repeatable development fixtures while preserving existing records.
- [Auth and policies](backend/auth-and-policies.md): Enforce account, row, action and field access on the server.
- [Transactional business rules](backend/graph-business-rules.md): Prepare a typed candidate graph while preserving validation, authorization and idempotency.
- [Durable effects](backend/durable-effects.md): Commit application effects with a graph save and deliver them through a retryable outbox.
- [Search and export](backend/search-and-export.md): Use typed search sources and export authorized records with a shared display policy.
- [Uploads and storage wiring](backend/uploads-and-storage-wiring.md): Turn a file column into an upload endpoint and choose a storage driver with one environment variable.
- [Middleware](backend/middleware.md): Read the Shelf pipeline around the generated router: logging, CORS, JSON defaults, error mapping and auth.
- [Extending Beak](extending/index.md): Drop to Flutter through a typed escape hatch when configuration runs out, without forking Beak.
- [Custom columns](extending/custom-columns.md): Render a table or detail cell with any obers_ui widget by pairing a @Custom field with a registered renderer.
- [Custom blocks and widgets](extending/custom-blocks-and-widgets.md): Embed custom widgets while sharing Beak's data, formatting, refresh and draft infrastructure.
- [Custom data sources](extending/custom-data-sources.md): Implement the ten methods of BeakDataSource to back Beak with any store, prove it with the shipped contract suite, and keep the Serverpod seam open.
- [Model-owned transports](extending/model-transports.md): Bind an existing backend to Beak models, share live permissions, and configure commands and archive actions without duplicating panel wiring.
- [Custom storage drivers](extending/custom-storage-drivers.md): Implement BeakStorageDriver's six members, hide the wire behind a thin transport seam, and register the driver so an environment variable selects it.
- [Using Beak widgets standalone](extending/using-beak-widgets-standalone.md): Embed Beak's forms, tables and data blocks in an existing Flutter application.
- [Testing and shipping](shipping/index.md): Test a Beak project, then ship it: configuration, production images, security and performance.
- [Testing](shipping/testing.md): Test declarative configuration, custom widgets and authoritative workflows at their actual boundaries.
- [Performance](shipping/performance.md): See how Beak keeps query counts low and where to look when a page is slow.
- [Security](shipping/security.md): Close the security seams of a Beak backend: guards, policies, row scopes, uploads and CORS.
- [Environment and config](shipping/environment-and-config.md): Set the environment variables a Beak backend reads and see how the environment wins over the .env file.
- [Going to production](shipping/going-to-production.md): Build the API and panel, run migrations, and configure production state explicitly.
- [Recipes](recipes/index.md): Find a maintained configuration for a common admin task.

- [Client bridge](serverpod/bridge/index.md): Use Beak on the client of an existing Serverpod project over your own DTO endpoints.
- [Bridge resources](serverpod/bridge/resources.md): Declare a ServerpodResource over your endpoints and know its limits.
- [Generating bridge resources](serverpod/bridge/generator.md): Generate bridge resources from a Serverpod client with beak_serverpod_generator.
- [Endpoint conventions](serverpod/bridge/endpoint-conventions.md): Look up the endpoint signatures and the query DTO vocabulary the bridge expects.
- [Authentication and scopes](serverpod/authentication.md): Wire Serverpod authentication into the Beak panel with scopes and the auth adapter.
- [Version compatibility](serverpod/versions.md): Look up which Beak versions match which Serverpod versions, and the exact pins.
- [Troubleshooting](serverpod/troubleshooting.md): Find the cause and the fix for common Serverpod integration errors.

## Reference

- [Reference](reference/index.md): Look up any annotation, field type, rule, block, option, REST route, CLI command or exception.
- [Cheatsheet](reference/cheatsheet.md): Find the configuration entrypoint for each common task.
- [Annotations](reference/annotations.md): Look up every annotation a schema class can carry, what it changes and where it applies.
- [Field types](reference/field-types.md): Look up every column type, the Dart type it is declared as, its options and its defaults.
- [Validation rules](reference/validation-rules.md): Look up every validation rule, its arguments, what it checks and the message it emits.
- [Behavior and actions](reference/behavior-and-actions.md): Look up the model behavior and action types with their fields and defaults.
- [Generated files and symbols](reference/generated-files.md): Look up the files beak prepare writes and the symbols generated for each schema.
- [Input builders](reference/input-builders.md): Look up the input builders you can call on a typed field in a form.
- [Filter builders](reference/filter-builders.md): Look up the filter builders you can call on a typed field in a list.
- [Screens and form layouts](reference/screens-and-layouts.md): Look up the resource screens and the form layout nodes with their options.
- [Blocks](reference/blocks.md): Look up every block type and its typed options.
- [Queries](reference/queries.md): Look up the query specification, filters, operators and typed values.
- [Panel and resource options](reference/panel-options.md): Look up every option of the panel, of a resource, of authentication, maintenance mode and formatting.
- [beak.yaml](reference/beak-yaml.md): Look up every key of the project file and what happens when you leave it out.
- [Configuration and environment](reference/configuration.md): Look up every environment variable and every backend and storage configuration field, with defaults.
- [CLI commands](reference/cli-commands.md): Look up every beak command, its flags, the files it writes and its exit codes.
- [REST API](reference/rest-api.md): Look up every endpoint the backend generates, with request bodies, responses and the error envelope.
- [Exceptions](reference/exceptions.md): Look up the exception family, each stable code, its HTTP status and when Beak throws it.
- [Libraries](reference/libraries.md): Look up the libraries of package:beak, what each is for and what it may import.
- [Packages](reference/packages.md): Look up the packages behind Beak, what each owns and which ones an app installs.
- [Glossary](reference/glossary.md): Look up one-line definitions of Beak vocabulary, cross-linked to the page that explains each.

- [Source map](ai/source-map.md): Find, for a symbol or area, the library to import, the source file and its test.

## Optional

- [Contributing](contributing/index.md): Get from a fresh clone to a green gate and learn the commands every change must pass.
- [Code guardrails](contributing/code-guardrails.md): Read the hard rules a change must satisfy: no Material, no type escape hatches and the layering.
- [Conventions](contributing/conventions.md): Follow the softer rules a reviewer looks for: commits, reuse, const and final, typed exceptions and tests.
- [Writing tests](contributing/writing-tests.md): Find where tests live per package, the harness each one uses and the coverage floor.
- [Writing docs](contributing/writing-docs.md): Write and check docs pages: the style guide, page templates, snippets and the docs gate.
- [Releasing](contributing/releasing.md): Cut a release: versions, the changelog, the obers_ui pin and the docs bundle.
- [Dev infrastructure](contributing/dev-infrastructure.md): Run the optional local Postgres and MinIO stack and know which suites need it.
- [Working with obers_ui](contributing/working-with-obers-ui.md): Pin obers_ui by git commit and develop against a local checkout when you need to.
- [Architecture](architecture/index.md): See how Beak is built inside: the principles, the package graph, the two flows and the seams.
- [Principles](architecture/principles.md): Read the invariants every part of Beak obeys, from define-once to no lazy loading, and why.
- [Package graph](architecture/package-graph.md): See which package depends on which and where worm and obers_ui may appear.
- [Backend flow](architecture/backend-flow.md): Follow a request through Handler, Service and DataSource and the single error catch boundary.
- [Frontend flow](architecture/frontend-flow.md): Follow the Widget, ViewModel, Repository and DataSource path, Signals state and the result boundary.
- [The query contract](architecture/query-contract.md): See how the query spec, filters and values serialize losslessly and become a worm query.
- [Graph commits](architecture/graph-commits.md): See how a graph save is planned, validated, committed transactionally and receipted.
- [The data source seam](architecture/data-source-seam.md): See how BeakDataSource lets the panel and the server run the same operations over worm, HTTP and Serverpod.
- [Code generation](architecture/code-generation.md): See how beak prepare discovers schemas, reads them and emits code and migrations.
- [Block system internals](architecture/block-system-internals.md): See how one sealed block union and a single host render pages, view modes, detail views and forms.
- [Storage internals](architecture/storage-internals.md): See how a storage config resolves to a driver and how the validator and transform pipeline run.
